stem: What normally causes functional closure of the foramen ovale after birth?

options.text: Increased left atrial pressure together with decreased right atrial pressure
Reduced umbilical venous return causing passive collapse over 3 to 7 days
Increased oxygen tension causing thrombosis and fibrosis within weeks
Slow loss of right ventricular dominance through childhood

explanation: Increased left atrial pressure together with decreased right atrial pressure is the normal mechanism for functional closure of the foramen ovale after birth.
rationale: Foramen ovale closure is pressure-driven at birth; left atrial pressure rises while right atrial pressure falls.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the rise in left atrial pressure and fall in right atrial pressure presses the septal flap closed.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because reduced umbilical venous return relates to closure of the ductus venosus, not the foramen ovale.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because increased oxygen tension is part of ductus arteriosus closure, not the foramen ovale.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because loss of right ventricular dominance is not the direct mechanism of functional foramen ovale closure.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because viral triggering of vasculitis is unrelated to postnatal foramen ovale closure.
